newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish govt sees more room for spending 1999/2000.
newsitem.headline: Swedish govt sees more room for spending 1999/2000.

text.p: The Swedish government's budget due later on Tuesday will include plans to spend an extra 15 billion crowns in 1999 and 26 billion crowns in 2000 on social reform measures, Swedish news agency TT reported.
The spending will be in addition to a five-point spending programme to be published in the budget, due to be issued at 1100 GMT. The budget was leaked by TT.

The government did not state exactly what the money would be used for, but said it would involve transferring money from the state to the private sector and would be aimed at improving justice and equality, TT reported.
The plans would involve some relief for Swedish companies, TT said.
The government will announce in the budget that it plans to spend 20 billion crowns by the end of 1998 on a five-point programme to restore the balance after two years of tough austerity measures.
